caption:
An AI just watched my video like a brain — and told me it wouldn't hit, before a single stranger saw it.

That's the pitch behind Higgsfield AI's newest feature, Virality Predictor, which shipped back in May. Higgsfield is already the engine behind a huge chunk of those impossible-camera-move, explosion-transition clips flooding your feed — it aggregates 30+ underlying AI video models (the tech that turns a prompt into footage) into one-tap cinematic presets. But Virality Predictor is a different kind of feature. It doesn't just generate video. It grades it.

Feed it a clip under 15 seconds and it maps a simulated viewer's attention, memory, and emotional response across the footage, then hands you a virality score, a peak hook timestamp, a hold rate, and a heatmap showing exactly which moments held attention and which lost it. One tracked test found a 7,000-view video scoring higher than a 2.1-million-view one — proof it's reading your footage on its own terms, not just parroting what already blew up.

It replaces the worst part of posting: filming something, publishing it blind, and refreshing the view count for two hours wondering if the first three seconds killed it. Now that guesswork happens before you hit publish.

The library of Viral Presets (think 'Red Carpet,' 'Neon City,' high-energy transitions) and Draw-to-Video, which turns a rough sketch into a full animated clip, mean this isn't only for people chasing ad performance — it's genuinely fun to poke around in.

Worth saying plainly: the 'brain' watching your video is a modeled simulation, not real audience data, so treat the score as a smart signal, not a promise. Higgsfield also built Soul Cast, a compliance tool restricting likeness uploads, after real backlash over how reference images were being used — a fair thing to know going in.

Save this so you don't lose it, and give Virality Predictor a run on your next clip before you post it blind. Full breakdown — link in bio.
